drafted_from: tools/export-documents-to-files/tool-rows.json (tool:write-a-web-page-from-a-record), do-work/render-public-page-cli.mjs, test/write-a-web-page.test.mjs, and a run of the command on the envelope below
start_here: Say to your AI: "Write the web page for my rye loaf record at bakery.example.com from this envelope file, and save it as page.html." It writes the envelope from the record, runs the page writer on your computer and tells you the address and where the file is.
no_lists_because: It reads one record that arrives inside the envelope file and writes one HTML file, so it names no list of yours.
instructions: 1. Clone the Workshop checkout and open a terminal in its root; the page writer needs only node.

2. Save the record and how to publish it as envelope.json: publication_descriptor (title, description and section fields, the address pieces), source_record (ref, revision_ref, fields) and materialized_values (the domain).

3. Say to your AI: "Write the web page from envelope.json to page.html". It reads the row with tools:list and runs node tools/export-documents-to-files/do-work/render-public-page-cli.mjs envelope.json page.html.

4. Read the last JSON line: artifact.canonical_url is the address the page is written for, artifact.byte_length its size, proof names the descriptor, record and revision, written is the file. Putting it on a site is a separate step you ask for.

worked_examples.title: A rye loaf record becomes a page for bakery.example.com
worked_examples.ask: Write the web page for my rye loaf record from envelope.json to page.html.
worked_examples.given: Run by the command: node tools/export-documents-to-files/do-work/render-public-page-cli.mjs envelope.json page.html. The envelope holds descriptor ref descriptor:article with a title from fields.title, a description from fields.summary, a paragraph section from fields.summary and a list section from fields.items; url scheme https, domain read from materialized_values site.domain (bakery.example.com), path segment read from fields.slug; source_record ref record:loaf-1, revision_ref revision:1, fields {title "Our Rye Loaf", slug "rye-loaf", summary "A dense rye loaf baked fresh each morning.", items ["rye flour","water","salt"]}; correlation_id correlation:bakery-1. Observed by running the command on this envelope in a scratch folder (the behaviour is also asserted in test/write-a-web-page.test.mjs).
